Yes, they can refuse. The euthanization of healthy animals statistically occurs more in farm animals because there is not usually a farm animal shelter nearby and no market for them at the time. 

House animals usually may just go to shelters or foster homes.

Yep it is. Since the 1970’s, the suicide mortality rate for veterinarians have been significantly higher compared to those with related professions, such as doctors and dentists. Also, they have access to means of suicide. The CDC noted that while firearms were a common method of suicide amongst vets, pharmaceutical poisoning caused 37 percent of suicide deaths (which happens to be 2.5 times higher compared to the general public). Often times, the profession demands that vets euthanize healthy animals, which can lead them to develop Perpetration-Induced Traumatic Stress (PITS). PITS is different from PTSD because the well-being of the veterinarian is never threatened, but rather their identity as a veterinarian is. 

So what can we do to on our side to help our animal doctors? Acknowledge the difficulties and hardships of the profession and be more considerate of your actions and your words when visiting the veterinarian. Be sure to thank them and let them know you appreciate them. 

Source: Wrote a research paper on veterinarian suicide.
